title: Pre-Analysis — Trim Air Zone Regulation Standard 2, First Round
abstract: First round of pre-analysis on extending the standard 2 trim air regulation to the remaining in-service population, closed with a rejection of the proposed effectivity after the duct flange condition survey.

sections.objective: Establish whether the standard 2 regulation could be offered to the whole remaining in-service population rather than only to aircraft already at the hardened seat standard, as three operators had asked. The question was one of effectivity rather than of design: the modification itself was released and flying, and the round was opened to test whether the pre-modification condition could be dropped.
sections.findings_summary: Three items were confirmed and together they closed the question. The earlier hardened seat standard is not merely a convenience: the standard 2 valve seats against a housing that the earlier modification keys, and on an unkeyed housing the new valve carrier can rotate under thermal cycling. The pre-conversion inspection bulletin exists precisely because the duct outlet flange has to be fit to carry a welded sensor boss, and a survey of ninety in-service ducts found eleven with local dressing that would not accept the weld; extending effectivity would have put those aircraft into a bulletin they cannot complete. The parts figure carries the two valve standards as alternates on separate sheets and its effectivity note would have had to be rewritten in a way that no longer matched the physical population. The round was closed with the pre-modification condition retained.
sections.next_steps: Retain the post-hardened-seat condition on the conversion bulletin. Tell the three requesting operators that the earlier bulletin is the route and that its kit is short lead. Re-open the analysis only if a housing keying method that can be applied in situ becomes available.

expected_findings.rationale: The standard 2 valve seats against a housing that the earlier modification keys. On an unkeyed housing the new carrier can rotate under thermal cycling, which is the failure the earlier modification was released to stop.
expected_findings.resolution: Retain the post-modification condition on the conversion bulletin.

expected_findings.rationale: The pre-conversion inspection exists because the duct outlet flange must be fit to carry a welded boss. Eleven of ninety surveyed ducts carried local dressing that will not accept the weld, so an extended effectivity would enrol aircraft that cannot complete the bulletin.
expected_findings.resolution: Do not extend the effectivity; keep the inspection as the gate.

expected_findings.rationale: The figure carries the two valve standards as alternates on separate sheets. An extended effectivity would require an effectivity note that no longer matched the physical population.
expected_findings.resolution: No change; the figure stays as issued because the effectivity is not extended.

type_data.conclusion: Closed with the effectivity unchanged. The housing keying and the duct flange condition both make the earlier modification a genuine prerequisite rather than an administrative one.
